nodes.name: Confined Atom Escape and Nucleation (CAEN)
nodes.procedure: The designed confined Ir atomic materials (Ir_CA) were subjected to high-temperature thermal treatment at 1000°C for 6h in a reducing hydrogen atmosphere. The confined Ir atoms underwent escaping from asymmetric N,O-coordination sites, diffusion, and controlled nucleation/aggregation on the nitrogen, oxygen-doped carbon matrix, forming uniformly distributed Ir nanoparticles (~3 nm) with fcc metallic Ir phase.

nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) and High-Resolution Transmission Electron Microscopy (HRTEM) analyses display a fluffy and porous structure of the obtained Ir_CA and no Ir-involved nanoparticles were observed...

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM of Ir_CAEN-1000-6 shows support carbon porous structure with locally curved graphitization zones d≈0.34 nm (graphite (002)), Ir lattice spacing 2.2Å matching (111) plane, FFT confirms (111)/(200) metallic Ir planes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HRTEM image of the Ir_CAEN-1000-6 catalyst (Figure 2c) also shows that the support carbon has a porous structure with locally curved graphitization zones with an interplanar distance ≈ 0.34 nm , corresponding to the graphite (002) plane. The lattice spacing with the width of 2.2Å is matched with the (111) plane of Ir...

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM demonstrates uniform size and homogeneous distribution of Ir nanoparticles (~3 nm) with residual confined Ir atoms visible as smaller white spots.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HADDF-STEM shown in Figure 2d further demonstrates that the Ir nanoparticles exhibit uniform size and homogeneous distribution. Figure 2e demonstrates that the particle size of Ir nanoparticles is ≈ 3 nm...

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping shows uniform distribution of C, O, N, and Ir elements without aggregation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The corresponding elemental mapping (Figure 2g) signifies the homogeneous distribution of Ir, C, N, and O elements...

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms N-Ir-O coordination in Ir_CA (Ir4+ at 62.5/65.4 eV); Ir_CAEN-1000-6 shows metallic Ir0 (61.0/63.9 eV) with reduced Ir-N/Ir-O peaks; O1s: Ir-O (531.9 eV), C-O (532.5 eV), O=C-O (533.4 eV); N1s: Ir-N (398.4 eV), pyrrolic (400.1 eV), graphitic (401.1 eV), oxidized N (403.3 eV).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution Ir 4f spectrum of Ir_CA (Figure S9d, Supporting Information) displays two characteristic peaks at 65.4 and 62.5 eV assigned to Ir 4f5/2 and Ir 4f7/2 of Ir4+ , respectively. The high-resolution Ir 4f spectrum of Ir_CAEN-1000-6 exhibits a new pair peaks at 61.0 and 63.9 eV assigned to Ir 4f5/2 and Ir 4f7/2 of Ir0...

nodes.characterization_summary: Aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM shows isolated bright spots confirming well-dispersed confined Ir single atoms in carbon framework.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The morphology analysis of Ir_CA material with sub-angstrom resolution was performed by using Aberration-Corrected High-Angle Annular Dark-Field Scanning TEM (AC HAADF-STEM). As depicted in Figure S8 (Supporting Information), the large number of isolated bright spots marked with yellow circles clearly shows that confined Ir atoms are well dispersed...

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows Ir_CA has only broad carbon peaks (no Ir crystalline phases); Ir_CAEN series develop fcc metallic Ir peaks with increasing crystallinity; Ir_CAEN-1000-6 shows sharp peaks at 40.6°(111), 47.3°(200), 69.1°(220), 83.4°(311) (PDF#87-0715).
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-Ray Diffraction (XRD) analysis, as depicted in Figure 3a, illustrates the phase transformation process of Ir in the samples under various thermal treatment conditions... Ir_CAEN-1000-6 shows all characteristic peaks at 40.6° , 47.3° , 69.1° , and 83.4° , which can be attributed to the (111), (200), (220), and (311) planes, respectively (PDF #87-0715).

nodes.characterization_summary: All catalysts contain ≈4.89 wt.% Ir content.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The measurements revealed that all prepared catalysts contained ≈ 4.89 wt.% Ir content...

nodes.characterization_summary: BET method measures specific surface area of Ir_CA and Ir_CAEN catalysts; surface area continuously increases with thermal treatment temperature/duration due to vacancy defect formation from Ir atom escape.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The N2 adsorption-desorption isotherm of the Ir_CA and Ir_CAEN catalyst displays a typical type IV characteristic hysteresis loop (Figure S11, Supporting Information), confirming the presence of mesopores inside the catalyst powder, which results in a large surface area (Figure 3c), measured by Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) method.

nodes.characterization_summary: BJH analysis shows hierarchical porous structure with pore size distributions at 3.5 nm and 10 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Barrett-Joyner-Halenda (BJH) analysis (Figure S12, Supporting Information) further shows that the all catalysts have a hierarchical porous structure with pore size distributions located at 3.5 and 10 nm , respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra show hydroxyl bending vibration at ≈1030 cm⁻¹ (δ(*OH)*O₂) and O-O stretching of gaseous O₂ at 1617 cm⁻¹ during OER.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman spectra of the OER process in the applied potential range of 0.85 - 1.65 V (Figure 5d,e) exhibit a transmittance peak at ≈ 1030 cm⁻¹ , characteristic of the bending vibration of hydroxyl.
